name: Tree Graph
description: Branching flow topology with minimal redundancy. Appears in vascular networks, river deltas, lightning paths, neural dendrites, and file systems. Optimizes distribution from source to many endpoints via minimum-path load balancing.

scope.definition: Agreement between branching tube radii in biological vascular networks and Murray's Law (r_parent³ = r₁³ + r₂³) — measured as fraction of branching points within 10% of Murray prediction.

evidence.source: Murray (1926) 'The physiological principle of minimum work', PNAS 12:207-214; Sherman (1981) 'On connecting large vessels to small', Journal of General Physiology 78:431-453.
cross_domain_examples: human bronchial tree: 0.88 of branching points within 10% of Murray's Law prediction
mammalian vascular tree: Murray's Law holds from aorta (25 mm) to capillary (5 µm) — 4 orders of magnitude
plant xylem branching: West-Brown-Enquist model (generalization of Murray) predicts metabolic scaling from branching
river drainage networks: Horton-Strahler branching ratios follow similar geometric scaling rules

scope.falsifiability: If measured vascular branching radii deviate from Murray's Law by >30% across all branching orders, the minimum-work principle is not the organizing constraint.
scope.measurement_limits: Murray's Law assumes laminar flow and Poiseuille resistance — fails in large vessels where turbulent flow dominates. Pulmonary arteries deviate from Murray's Law because equal pressure drop (not work) is optimized.
